step1_analysis.description: A CMOS inverter with exposed source terminals, acting as a delay element. It is likely part of a current-starved delay line used in a time-to-digital converter, where the delay is controlled by a temperature-dependent current.

paper_reference.title: A Time-to-Digital-Converter-Based CMOS Smart Temperature Sensor

sky130_expected.calculation: t_pd = C_load * VDD / (2 * I_avg). With C_load=50fF, I_dn ~ 2.5mA, I_dp ~ 0.47mA, t_pd_hl ~ 18ps, t_pd_lh ~ 95ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on SKY130 mobility and threshold voltages with a 50fF load. The PMOS is weaker than the NMOS due to equal sizing, leading to asymmetric delays.
NMOS is much stronger than PMOS due to equal sizing (W=5u) and higher electron mobility, shifting V_th below VDD/2 (0.9V).

sky130_expected.calculation: P = C * VDD^2 * f. At 50MHz with 50fF load, P = 50f * 1.8^2 * 50e6 = 8.1uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dynamic power dominates. Scaled to a 50MHz testbench frequency to match the order of magnitude of the paper's reported power while keeping simulation time short.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure propagation delay, switching threshold, and power consumption of the delay element.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Delay Element Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u

XM2 OUT IN N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM7 OUT IN N2 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}

* Supply and Bias Connections (Tying exposed sources to rails for standard inverter operation)
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VN2 N2 0 1.8
VN4 N4 0 0

* Input Signal (50 MHz)
VIN IN 0 PULSE(0 1.8 5n 0.1n 0.1n 10n 20n)

* Load Capacitor
CL OUT 0 50f

.control
* DC Analysis for Switching Threshold
dc VIN 0 1.8 0.01
meas dc v_th when v(out)=0.9 rise=1

* Transient Analysis for Delay and Power
tran 10p 40n
meas tran t_rise trig v(out) val=0.36 rise=1 targ v(out) val=1.44 rise=1
meas tran t_fall trig v(out) val=1.44 fall=1 targ v(out) val=0.36 fall=1
meas tran t_pd_hl trig v(in) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran t_pd_lh trig v(in) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 rise=1
let t_pd = (t_pd_hl + t_pd_lh) / 2
print t_pd

* Power Measurement
let inst_power = -i(VVDD)*1.8 - i(VN2)*1.8
meas tran avg_power avg inst_power from=0 to=40n

quit
.endc
.end
